external.greybook is the CERN Greybook experiment code as used in the URL greybook.cern.ch/greybook/experiment/detail?id=NA62; the Greybook page itself is a client-rendered app and could not be fetched for a verbatim quote this session.

Membership counts (institutions/countries/participants) are deliberately left off both here and on collaboration:na62: the official collaboration page (na62.web.cern.ch/Collaboration/organisationalStructure.html) links to the Greybook for the member list but states no headline number itself, and a per-brief rule requires the collaboration's own page as the source for any membership count. A widely repeated figure (~300 participants, ~33 institutions, ~16 countries) appears in secondary aggregations but was not confirmed on a page fetched this session, so it is not recorded.

The 2026-03-04 CERN news article (src:na62-cern-news-2026-refined-measurement) first previewed a refined branching-ratio value from the 2026 La Thuile conference; a full arXiv preprint restating the identical value, arXiv:2607.16413 ('Measurement of the branching ratio of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay', submitted 17 July 2026, CERN-EP-2026-214), was found during 2026-09-17 verification and is now used to source result:na62-2026-refined-measurement's claim, since A16 forbids sourcing a result claim to a press release.

physics_goals.note: 2026-09-17 fixed-target verification: the previous quote dropped the page's leading 'NA62 initially proposed to' and capitalised 'measure' as if it opened the sentence, which is a spliced, non-verbatim quote (A15 requires the exact text seen). Corrected to the full sentence; note that the page itself frames the 10% figure as the *initial* proposed precision, not a claim about the precision actually achieved.
physics_goals.quote: NA62 initially proposed to measure the very rare kaon decay K+ -> pi+ nu nubar at the CERN SPS to extract a 10% measurement of the CKM parameter |Vtd|.
physics_goals.value: Measure the branching ratio of the very rare kaon decay K+ -> pi+ nu nubar to extract a percent-level measurement of the CKM matrix element |Vtd| and test the Standard Model

summary.plain: NA62 is a CERN experiment that fires a beam of charged kaons at a detector to catch one of the rarest particle decays known: a positive kaon turning into a pion and two invisible neutrinos. Catching enough of these decays tests the Standard Model.
summary.technical: Fixed-target kaon-decay experiment in the ECN3 cavern of the CERN SPS North Area, using a 400 GeV/c primary proton beam to produce a secondary/tertiary charged-kaon beam. Measures the branching ratio of K+ -> pi+ nu nubar via a decay-in-flight technique with GigaTracker beam-timing, RICH, LKr calorimeter and veto subsystems (arXiv:1703.08501). Constructed 2009-2014, commissioned 2014-2015, Run 1 data 2016-2018 (arXiv:2103.15389, 3.4 sigma evidence-level measurement), Run 2 from 2021 with upgraded beam intensity, reaching a 5 sigma observation with 2016-2022 data (arXiv:2412.12015) and a further refined measurement including 2023-2024 data reported in 2026.

unique_capabilities.note: The 750 MHz beam-rate figure is the widely-cited design value; it is NOT included as a key_spec because no source fetched this session states it verbatim, only the GigaTracker's flux-handling and timing figures were confirmed by direct fetch.
unique_capabilities.value: A decay-in-flight technique using a high-intensity (~750 MHz) unseparated hadron beam and precision timing (the GigaTracker beam spectrometer reaches 65 ps time resolution on tracks) to identify K+ -> pi+ nu nubar events against enormous backgrounds
